title: Three-Week IB Geography Revision Plan for November
summary: IB Geography revision plan for November: organise three focused weeks of topic triage, active recall, timed practice, feedback, and protected rest.
body_markdown:
November examinations create a peculiar kind of pressure. The calendar says there is still time, but students balancing several IB subjects know how quickly three weeks can disappear.


The best response is not to study Geography all day. It is to make each session answer a specific question: What do I know? What can I apply? What still breaks down under time pressure?


This three-week **IB Geography revision plan** moves through those questions in order. Week one diagnoses and rebuilds knowledge. Week two turns knowledge into geographical arguments. Week three rehearses the examination while protecting sleep and attention. Adapt the schedule around your subjects, school commitments and Geography level.


### Your three-week overview


Week Main priority Geography workload Desired outcome


Week one Topic triage and active recall 45-75 minutes on most days Identify gaps and rebuild essential knowledge


Week two Application and timed questions 60-90 minutes on selected days Produce clearer evidence-based answers


Week three Exam rehearsal and recovery Short timed sessions plus one or two full simulations Improve pacing without arriving exhausted


Before starting, gather your course outline, teacher feedback, class notes, case studies, calculator where relevant and permitted, and approved practice material. RevisionDojo can keep these activities connected through its[IB learning resources](https://www.revisiondojo.com/ib) , including Study Notes, Flashcards, AI Chat, grading tools and exam-style practice.


A student faces a calendar-shaped mountain and asks whether revision counts as fieldwork while a rest bench waits halfway up


*Even the most ambitious revision climb needs a rest stop.*


### Week one: triage the Geography syllabus


The first week is not about covering everything equally. Equal time feels organised, but it can be wasteful. A topic you can already explain accurately needs less attention than one you recognise only when your notes are open.


Create a topic audit using three categories:


- **Green:** I can define key terms, explain processes and use specific evidence.
- **Amber:** I understand the topic but struggle to recall examples or build an argument.
- **Red:** I cannot explain the topic confidently without support.


Do this separately for core content, your studied options and, for HL students, the relevant extension material. Use the current course outline supplied by your teacher rather than an old online checklist, since requirements and taught options can vary.


### A realistic week-one rhythm


Spend the first day completing the audit. Over the next four or five days, alternate red and amber topics. A 60-minute session might contain:


- 10 minutes of retrieval without notes
- 20 minutes rebuilding one concept from[RevisionDojo Study Notes](https://www.revisiondojo.com/notes)
- 15 minutes creating or reviewing[active-recall Flashcards](https://www.revisiondojo.com/flashcards)
- 15 minutes answering one focused question


Geography knowledge becomes useful when it is attached to place, scale and consequence. For every case study, reduce your notes to four anchors: location, process, precise supporting evidence and analytical significance. Avoid memorising disconnected numbers. A statistic is valuable only if you know what claim it supports.


Keep at least one evening free from Geography. If you are sitting several November subjects, assign your longest sessions to whichever examination is closest or weakest. A plan should reduce decision fatigue, not compete with every other subject for first place.


### Week two: turn knowledge into geographical answers


In week two, shift from reviewing content to producing answers. Many students mistake familiarity for readiness. A page can look obvious when open and vanish when the clock starts.


Begin each session with a question rather than a chapter. Use the[RevisionDojo Questionbank](https://www.revisiondojo.com/questionbank) to select questions by topic and difficulty. Complete shorter items first, then progress to extended responses that require evaluation, comparison or judgement.


### Use a question-feedback-retry loop


For every substantial response:


1. Read the command term and identify exactly what the question requires.
2. Set a time limit appropriate to the marks and your teacher's guidance.
3. Answer without notes.
4. Compare your response with the mark guidance or submit it to RevisionDojo's grading tools.
5. Record one content problem and one technique problem.
6. Rewrite the weakest paragraph within 24 hours.


This final step matters. Reading feedback can create the impression of improvement, but rewriting forces the correction into practice.


For extended answers, plan a defensible position before writing. Each paragraph should connect a claim, geographical reasoning, evidence and the question. Evaluation should not be confined to a final sentence. Consider scale, time, stakeholders, uncertainty and exceptions throughout the response.


If you become stuck,[RevisionDojo AI Chat](https://www.revisiondojo.com/) can help clarify a process or test your understanding. Ask it to question you rather than simply reveal an answer. The goal is productive difficulty, not effortless completion.


### Schedule around other November subjects


Choose three or four serious Geography sessions this week rather than promising yourself seven. One possible pattern is:


- Monday: weak core topic and short questions
- Wednesday: option topic and one extended response
- Friday: mixed timed set
- Sunday: review errors and update case-study flashcards


On days dominated by another subject, complete only 10-15 minutes of Geography retrieval. Small maintenance sessions prevent knowledge from becoming cold without consuming the evening.


### Week three: rehearse, refine and rest


The final week is where students often abandon sensible planning. Anxiety makes new notes feel productive, so they start rebuilding the course from page one. Resist that urge.


Your priorities are now timing, selection and composure. Sit one or two timed papers or carefully constructed mixed sets in[RevisionDojo Exam mode](https://www.revisiondojo.com/) . Use the format and timing confirmed by your teacher for your current examination session and level. Complete the work under realistic conditions, with only the materials permitted in the examination.


After each simulation, sort mistakes into four groups:


Error type Corrective action


Knowledge gap Review the smallest relevant section and retrieve it again later


Weak evidence Add one usable place-specific example to your case-study bank


Misread command term Rewrite the question as a simple instruction


Timing problem Practise planning and stopping at fixed checkpoints


Do not immediately sit another complete paper. Analysis is where the learning occurs. Use RevisionDojo's Mock Exams or Predicted Papers for fresh timed material, then revisit related Questionbank items where the diagnosis shows a recurring weakness.


### The final 72 hours


Reduce volume as the examination approaches. Review concise case-study sheets, recurring mistakes, definitions and planning structures. Avoid introducing large new topics unless they are essential and clearly examinable.


Protect sleep, regular meals and short periods away from screens. Rest is not time stolen from revision. It is part of the system that allows recall, judgement and writing speed to survive examination day.


The evening before the exam, prepare what you need, check the official time and location communicated by your school, and stop at a reasonable hour. A tired extra hour rarely compensates for a distracted morning.


### Make the plan flexible, not fragile


A three-week schedule will not unfold perfectly. A difficult Chemistry task may take an evening. A school deadline may appear. You may discover that an amber topic is actually red.


Build one unassigned buffer session into each week. If nothing goes wrong, use it for mixed retrieval or rest. If a day is lost, move the essential task into the buffer instead of compressing several sessions into one punishing night.


The deeper lesson is simple: good revision is a feedback system. Diagnose, practise, inspect and adjust. RevisionDojo brings that cycle together through the Questionbank, Study Notes, Flashcards, AI Chat, grading tools, Predicted Papers, Mock Exams, Coursework Library and Tutors. Start with targeted practice in the Questionbank, then enter Exam mode when you are ready to make time pressure part of the lesson.
